entries.note: A Chinese-style inn or tavern common in wuxia settings.
A traditional term for a young male worker who serves guests at an inn.
A private room for lodging guests at an inn.
An organized school or lineage within the martial world.
Someone of exceptionally high skill, especially in martial arts.
An exalted title for a supreme swordsman.
A title for a peerless master of poisons and poison arts.
A mystical formation designed to send someone back into the past.
Here, the residual persona and memories of a master who died in the failed future.
The energy center in the lower abdomen where internal energy is stored and cultivated.
Cultivated inner power used to perform martial techniques.
The channels through which internal energy circulates in the body.
The outer, generally lower-ranking division of a martial sect.
A foundational sword art whose name invokes heaven, earth, and humanity.
A system or style of sword techniques.
A confidential or sealed message, often used between factions.
A legal claim over property used to secure a debt.
The person who initially held the debt before it was transferred.
A personal written mark used to authenticate a document.
A premodern local government office and its authorities.
A traditional unit of money; its value depends on the historical setting.
A board bearing the name of a building or institution.
A room used to store large fermentation jars and earthenware crocks.
The recognized authority to control or investigate a particular matter.
A trusted, higher-status disciple admitted to a sect’s inner school.
An official tablet or badge proving identity and sect affiliation.

entries.translation: the time it takes to eat a meal
entries.note: A traditional, approximate short span of time rather than a precise modern unit.
Can denote either physical poison in the air or the harmful force of a poison.
A concealed needle coated with or used to inject poison.
Martial or medical techniques centered on creating, controlling, or countering poison.
The poison responsible for the victim’s branching green-blue veins.
An additive that binds the poison to another substance or slows its absorption.
A fingerprint impressed on a document as identification or authorization.
A person trained in combat and martial disciplines.
The broader body of supernatural or cultivated fighting techniques in wuxia.
A formal term used here in the allegations of stealing a token and martial arts.
Literally a mountain gate; by extension, a martial sect’s home compound.
A younger or later-entering male disciple of the same martial lineage, not a biological brother.
An older or earlier-entering male disciple of the same martial lineage, not a biological brother.
A form specifically designed to counter or disrupt a sword technique.
Three discrete exchanges of attacks and counters in a martial bout.
The trajectory or intended line followed by a sword technique.
A deceptive technique that appears to be the true attack but is not.
A trained system of steps and body movement used in martial arts.
A respectful wuxia form of address for a young male martial artist.
An honorific for a respected martial artist, often used with a surname.
A traditional martial greeting made by enclosing one fist with the other hand.
Entrusting a task and the power to make decisions to someone else.
The owner or manager of an inn.
A fine needle used for examination, treatment, or as a concealed weapon.
Here, 돈 is a traditional unit of medicinal weight rather than money.
Here, 푼 is a small traditional unit of medicinal weight.
In this context, a closely guarded medical prescription—not ‘slander.’
A written record of sword techniques or sword-art teachings.
A prescribed combination and method for neutralizing poison.
A traditional time unit equal to roughly two modern hours; 반 시진 is about one hour.
A formally sealed written message, often carrying an order.
The recognized leader of a powerful family or martial clan.
A trap formation that drops blades when triggered.
Internal energy expressed through or as the cutting force of a sword.
Cultivated internal power; often used more broadly than 내공 in describing an active energy current.
A formation powered by or constructed from multiple martial-energy traditions.
The principles and techniques used to construct qi-powered arrays, traps, or ritual mechanisms.
The visible flash or luminous path produced by a swift sword strike.
The cutting gust or pressure generated by a sword technique.
A slogan expressing the imposition of one universal standard.
A powerful centralized faction within the martial world.
Ryu Dan’s original footwork for redirecting received force through the next step.
A carved wooden block used to print repeated text onto paper.
The jointly sealed ledger defining access to emergency procedures, medicine, routes, and responsibilities.
